title: The complete European guidelines on phenylketonuria: diagnosis and treatment
authors: van Wegberg AMJ, MacDonald A, Ahring K, Bélanger-Quintana A, Blau N, Bosch AM, et al.
funder: A grant from the European Society for Phenylketonuria and Allied Disorders (ESPKU) funded a project assistant; the ESPKU had no opportunity to influence the writing process. One group meeting and one plenary meeting were supported by Excemed.
authorConflicts: Most authors declared advisory-board membership, honoraria, grants or research funding from Merck Serono, BioMarin, Nutricia/Danone, Vitaflo International, Arla Foods, Recordati, Orphan Europe or Excemed; A. van Wegberg received a grant from the ESPKU.
result: Treat untreated blood phenylalanine above 600 umol/L; treat 360 to 600 umol/L during the first 12 years of life; patients aged 12 years or more with untreated phenylalanine below 600 umol/L do not require treatment; upper target 360 umol/L before 12 years and 600 umol/L from 12 years, lower target 120 umol/L; treatment for life recommended. The precise pathogenesis of brain dysfunction is still unclear; existing treatments aim at decreasing blood phenylalanine because high concentrations are strongly related to neurocognitive outcome.
